newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: U.S. Halliburton's Cheney in talks in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Halliburton's Cheney in talks in Bangladesh.

text.p: Former U.S. defence secretary Dick Cheney, who heads the Halliburton engineering company, held talks on Saturday in Bangladesh about his firm's investment in gas and oil exploration, energy ministry officials said.
They said Brown and Roots, a subsidiary of the Halliburton, had proposed to invest about $100 million for developing offshore gas field found by the Cairn Energy Plc of Britain.
"The U.S. company will join the Cairn to form a consortium," said one official.

Cairn, in Bangladesh under a production sharing contract, has already drilled two wells in the Bay of Bengal. The gas reserves have been estimated at roughly one trillion cubic feet of gas, the official said.
He said the company has already invested about $30 million.
The officials said the British company estimated $200 million would be required to develop the gas field and would form a consortium with Halliburton to share the cost.

The government was yet to approve the partnership deal. "We welcome Halliburton in Bangladesh. It's a big and reputed company. But we we are still examining the terms of the proposal," said Energy Secretary S. A. Samad.
Bangladesh has already a proven gas reserves of 10.2 trillion cubic feet.
Cheney, who arrived in Dhaka on Friday, held talks with Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad, Commerce and Industry Minister Tofael Ahmed and senior officials of the energy ministry.
